outcome: surgical wound dehiscence following Caesarean section
cohort: The study included 100 female patients who underwent caesarean section, with 50 patients experiencing wound dehiscence (cases) and 50 patients without wound dehiscence (controls).
finding: Increased BMI, irregularity of antenatal visits, prior Caesarean section, and intrapartum steroid use were identified as significant risk factors associated with the development of surgical wound dehiscence following Caesarean section.
mod_finding: A history of prior Caesarean section was associated with 1.5 times higher odds of developing wound dehiscence.
